intended_object: The coefficientwise action of a Galois automorphism σ ∈ Gal(L/k) on the base change L ⊗_k R, given by σ ⊗ id_R (l ⊗ r ↦ σ(l) ⊗ r), as a k-algebra endomorphism. Inferred from the docstring ("Coefficientwise Galois conjugation") and the lemmas `coefficientwise_tmul`, `coefficientwise_mul` and `fixed_iff_mem_range_includeRight`.
explanation:
The body is `Algebra.TensorProduct.map σ.toAlgHom (AlgHom.id k R)`. This is exactly σ ⊗ id_R as a k-algebra map L ⊗[k] R → L ⊗[k] R, so l ⊗ r ↦ σ l ⊗ r, which is the standard Galois action on the coefficients of the base change.

The generated API signature (docs/API.md) shows that Lean drops the unused section instances `[FiniteDimensional k L]` and `[IsGalois k L]`. The definition therefore only needs a field extension L/k, a k-algebra automorphism σ and a commutative k-algebra R. The library relies on this: it also applies the definition to infinite extensions K/k, for absolute Galois groups. Making L an arbitrary k-algebra would be more general still, but the definition is specifically "Galois conjugation", which is posed for field extensions, so that is not a meaningful restriction.

Mathlib has no dedicated named notion for this. The definition is a thin, correct specialization of the general tensor-product map `Algebra.TensorProduct.map` to the case relevant to Galois descent. Nothing is missing or wrong: the result is multiplicative in σ, and the identity automorphism acts as the identity.
